142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:

149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are

152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.

155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on

158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See

161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,

164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.

166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.

172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.

183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL

188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.

196

198

200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:

205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.

214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

Forgetting `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` makes 217 text on a brand button unreadable. 218 219 Better than hand-writing: generate the full set with the 220 [Themer](https://gravity-ui.com/themer) web tool or 221 [`@gravity-ui/uikit-themer`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit-themer) — both 222 recalculate the dependent palette from a single base color. 223 224 ### A section `ThemeProvider` with no provider above it themes the whole page 225 226 ❌ **Incorrect** — a dark widget mounted where no `ThemeProvider` (or v8 227 `Provider`) wraps it: an embedded widget, a micro-frontend, a separate React 228 root: 229 230 ```tsx 231 {/* no provider above → writes to document.body */} 232 233 234 ``` 235 236 ✓ **Correct**: 237 238 ```tsx 239 240 241 242 ``` 243 244 **Why:** only the outermost `ThemeProvider` writes the theme class to 245 `document.body` — globally, last-wins. One nested inside another 246 `ThemeProvider` (or a v8 `Provider`) is always scoped, with or without the prop, 247 so a dark section inside the app needs no `scoped`. With no provider above, 248 `scoped` renders a dedicated `
` around the 249 children *and* updates the theme React context (so `useTheme` inside the 250 section sees the section's theme). For a CSS-only region without context, apply 251 the class manually: `
`. 252 253 ### Controls on a brand/colored background: fixed contrast, both themes 254 255 ❌ **Incorrect** — default button on a brand-colored hero: 256 257 ```tsx 258
259 {/* default view follows theme → low contrast on bright bg */} 260
261 ``` 262 263 ✓ **Correct** — use a `*-contrast` view, which is built for a contrast 264 background, or scope a CSS override fixing contrast for both themes: 265 266 ```tsx 267
268 {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */} 269
270 ``` 271 272 **Why:** a brand-colored fill is usually the *same* color in light and dark 273 (it's a fill, not a themed surface), so the control on top should keep a fixed 274 contrast in both themes rather than lightening/darkening with the theme. 275 `normal-contrast` / `outlined-contrast` / `flat-contrast` do exactly that. 276 Do **not** reach for `raised` here — its surface is themed (light in light, 277 dark in dark), so it does not hold contrast on a fixed fill. If no `*-contrast` 278 view fits, override the component's CSS API (`--g-button-background-color`, 279 `--g-button-text-color`, …) scoped to the section, with contrast values for 280 both themes. This is distinct from `--g-color-text-brand-contrast`, which is 281 about text on a *brand button* (`view="action"`). 282 283 ### Customization ladder — descend only when there's no higher handle 284 285 When you need to change how a Gravity UI component looks, try in this order: 286 287 1. **Global tokens** (`--g-*` semantic tokens / theme) — change the look 288 everywhere by changing the token, not components one by one. 289 2. **Component's own CSS API** (`--g-button-*`, `--g-card-border-radius`, 290 `--g-text-input-*`, …) — scoped to the wrapper / class of the spot you're 291 changing. Check the component's README for the variables it exposes. 292 3. **A narrow, flagged hack** — a custom class on a specific internal element, 293 with a comment "hack on internal classes, pinned to version ", and a note 294 to upstream it. Only after confirming step 1 and 2 don't expose a handle. 295 4. **NEVER** broad structural matches: `[class*='…']` or ID selectors against 296 internal markup. Such an override is written against one specific DOM 297 structure and breaks silently when it changes. 298 299 **Why:** a `[class*='…']` override that worked yesterday breaks tomorrow when 300 the component adds a wrapper or renames an internal class — and you won't get a 301 type error, just a visually broken layout. Always start at the top of the 302 ladder; descend one rung only when the rung above has no handle. 303 304 --- 305 306 ## Color & shape 307 308 ### Use semantic tokens, never raw hex or private tokens 309 310 ❌ `color: #1677FF` 311 ❌ `background: var(--g-color-private-blue-500)` 312 ✓ `color: var(--g-color-text-link)` 313 ✓ `background: var(--g-color-base-brand)` 314 315 **Why:** Gravity UI's color system is two-layered. The *private* layer 316 (`--g-color-private--`) is the raw palette — an implementation 317 detail that can change, never reference it directly. The *semantic* layer 318 (`--g-color-{group}-{role}`) encodes intent and is theme-aware. Use it: 319 320 - backgrounds/fills: `--g-color-base-*` (`base-background`, `base-brand`, 321 `base-generic`, `base-danger-*`, …) 322 - text/icons: `--g-color-text-*` (`text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-hint`, 323 `text-brand`, `text-link`, …) 324 - borders/lines: `--g-color-line-*` (`line-generic`, `line-brand`, `line-focus`, 325 `line-danger`) 326 - effects: `--g-color-sfx-*` (`sfx-shadow`, `sfx-veil`, `sfx-fade`) 327 328 For text on a brand/colored background, use `--g-color-text-brand-contrast` 329 (not the plain brand color — it has no contrast guarantee). 330 331 ### Border radius uses a token, never a hard-coded `px` 332 333 ❌ `border-radius: 8px` 334 ✓ `border-radius: var(--g-border-radius-m)` 335 336 **Why:** the scale is `--g-border-radius-{xs|s|m|l|xl}`. Components expose 337 their own radius variable on the same scale (`--g-button-border-radius`, 338 `--g-card-border-radius`, `--g-modal-border-radius`, …) so you can tune one 339 component without moving the global scale. # @gravity-ui/markdown-editor documentation

Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/markdown-editor`.
Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.

Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/markdown-editor/build/docs/`).

## For AI agents

A dual-mode Markdown editor for React that combines a WYSIWYG mode (ProseMirror) and a raw markup mode (CodeMirror), with support for basic Markdown and YFM.

### When to use

- Editing Markdown/YFM content with a switchable visual (WYSIWYG) and source (markup) view.
- You need an extensible editor: custom marks, nodes, toolbar items, and extensions (HTML, LaTeX, Mermaid, GPT) via the ProseMirror/CodeMirror engines.
- Rendering the editor UI: create the instance with `useMarkdownEditor` and render it with `MarkdownEditorView`.

### When not to use

- Read-only rendering of Markdown to HTML with no editing — transform it with [`@diplodoc/transform`](https://github.com/diplodoc-platform/transform) and render the output instead.
- Plain multiline text input — use `TextArea` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
- Rich-text that is not Markdown/YFM — this editor is Markdown-first.

### Common pitfalls

- **It is a hook plus a view, not one component.** Create the instance with `useMarkdownEditor(...)` and pass it to `<MarkdownEditorView editor={editor} />`; there is no single `<MarkdownEditor>` you render directly.
- **Read the value via the instance, not a controlled `value` prop.** Call `editor.getValue()` (e.g. on the `submit` event) to serialize to Markdown; the editor manages its own state.
- **Peer dependencies are required.** Your project must provide `@diplodoc/transform`, `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/components`, `react`, and `react-dom` — check the `peerDependencies` in `package.json`.
- **Styles and i18n come from uikit.** Set up theming/styles per the uikit docs and call `configure({lang})` from both this package and `@gravity-ui/uikit`.

## Install

```shell
npm install @gravity-ui/markdown-editor
```

### Required dependencies

Please note that to start using the package, your project must also have the following installed: `@diplodoc/transform`, `react`, `react-dom`, `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/components` and some others. Check out the `peerDependencies` section of `package.json` for accurate information.

## Usage

The markdown editor is supplied as a React hook to create an instance of editor and a component for rendering the view.\
To set up styling and theme see [UIKit docs](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit?tab=readme-ov-file#styles).

```tsx

## For AI agents

A dual-mode Markdown editor for React that combines a WYSIWYG mode (ProseMirror) and a raw markup mode (CodeMirror), with support for basic Markdown and YFM.

### When to use

- Editing Markdown/YFM content with a switchable visual (WYSIWYG) and source (markup) view.
- You need an extensible editor: custom marks, nodes, toolbar items, and extensions (HTML, LaTeX, Mermaid, GPT) via the ProseMirror/CodeMirror engines.
- Rendering the editor UI: create the instance with `useMarkdownEditor` and render it with `MarkdownEditorView`.

### When not to use

- Read-only rendering of Markdown to HTML with no editing — transform it with [`@diplodoc/transform`](https://github.com/diplodoc-platform/transform) and render the output instead.
- Plain multiline text input — use `TextArea` from [`@gravity-ui/uikit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit).
- Rich-text that is not Markdown/YFM — this editor is Markdown-first.

### Common pitfalls

- **It is a hook plus a view, not one component.** Create the instance with `useMarkdownEditor(...)` and pass it to `<MarkdownEditorView editor={editor} />`; there is no single `<MarkdownEditor>` you render directly.
- **Read the value via the instance, not a controlled `value` prop.** Call `editor.getValue()` (e.g. on the `submit` event) to serialize to Markdown; the editor manages its own state.
- **Peer dependencies are required.** Your project must provide `@diplodoc/transform`, `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/components`, `react`, and `react-dom` — check the `peerDependencies` in `package.json`.
- **Styles and i18n come from uikit.** Set up theming/styles per the uikit docs and call `configure({lang})` from both this package and `@gravity-ui/uikit`.

## Install

```shell
npm install @gravity-ui/markdown-editor
```

### Required dependencies

Please note that to start using the package, your project must also have the following installed: `@diplodoc/transform`, `react`, `react-dom`, `@gravity-ui/uikit`, `@gravity-ui/components` and some others. Check out the `peerDependencies` section of `package.json` for accurate information.

    };

}
